body:
Marta: Quick design review — the version history timeline feels kinda endless on long rollouts. I prototyped a persistent date marker + mini scrubber. Screenshot: https://figma.com/file/xyz Sam: Love the scrubber idea, but need to avoid hiding the rollback CTA when users scroll. Priya: FWIW timeline is virtualized already; adding a sticky header is doable but could cause a jarring jump when new streaming events arrive. Carlos: Implementation note — use CSS `position: sticky` for date markers, but manage focus and aria-live carefully so screen readers don't get noisy. Ava: Accessibility: if the date marker is sticky, ensure keyboard focus can land on each timeline entry. Add offscreen labels like "Event at 09:32 — canary started" for assistive tech. Marta: Good call. Also proposing copy change: 'Canary rollout — 5% → 25% (automated)' instead of vague 'canary started'. Sam: +1 on explicit copy. Also prefer 'View rollback' -> 'Rollback to v2.1' for clarity. Carlos: For hover diff preview: render a small 2-line diff + 'View full diff' button. Avoid heavy DOM during scroll; lazy-render on hover/focus. Carlos: aria code snippet: ``
``` Marta: Thoughts on grouping micro-events? e.g., 3 tiny traffic adjustments within 5m condensed into '3 traffic adjustments' with expand chevron. Priya: Grouping helps perf and UX. We'll need an expand/collapse affordance that is keyboard and screen-reader accessible. Ava: Keyboard nav: arrow keys when the timeline container has focus, `Enter` to open details. Avoid global single-letter shortcuts like `k`/`j` unless discoverable. Sam: UX nit for mobile: rollback button should be in the details top-right; in narrow breakpoints collapse into a floating FAB labeled 'Rollback'. Marta: I'll update Figma frames with sticky markers, grouped events, and the hover preview states. Will include a compact/expanded toggle. deploy-bot: Mock uploaded: https://figma.com/proto/abcd — comments enabled Carlos: I'll spike the sticky marker + keyboard nav this week and pair with @Ava for a11y smoke tests. Priya: Perf note: cap client-side event buffering (e.g., archive older than 30 days or 10k events) to avoid memory growth. Marta: Great — I'll push copy changes + accessible labels by EOD and post updated frames. Thanks everyone :sparkles:
